# Workflow {background-color="#23373B"}

# Workflow

Workflow is a system to make it easier on your brain to do your work. Don't waste time finding things or trying to remember that great idea you had. We'll work toward something organized and systematic that ensures replicability and minimizes mistakes.

. . .

::: {.big}
A **keystone habit**: the one habit that organizes all the other good habits
:::

# Organizing Your Research {background-color="#23373B"}

# Project notebooks

Organize your projects into notebooks (or folders) of some kind. Digital options include OneNote, Evernote, Notion, Google Keep, or just text files in a folder. Bullet journals (pen and paper) work too.


# Project notebooks: my system

Three categories, and a project moves through them in order.

::::: {.flow}
:::: {.step}
💡

**Pending**

Ideas. A Google Keep note at first, then its own notebook or folder (on an e-ink tablet) once it has had some thought
::::
:::: {.arrow .fragment}
→
::::
:::: {.step .fragment}
🔬

**Ongoing**

Actual working projects. One section per project, with "meeting notes" (if co-authored) and "ideas/thoughts"
::::
:::: {.arrow .fragment}
→
::::
:::: {.step .fragment}
✅

**Completed**

Once the paper is officially accepted and all the supporting documentation is finalized
::::
:::::

::: {.notes}
Ask the room before revealing the flow: where do your half-formed ideas live right now? Phone notes, a notebook, nowhere?
:::


# Organizing One Project {background-color="#23373B"}

# Project folders

Key is to have a system where files are named appropriately and everything is easily accessible. Basically it's a closet for your research.


# Project folders

Every one of my projects starts from the same skeleton. A single command (`/kickoff-research`, a Claude Code skill) builds it, so no two projects are organized differently.

::: {.tree}
```
📁 project
├── 📄 README.md
├── 📁 paper/            paper.tex or paper.qmd, plus the bibliography
├── 📁 presentations/
├── 📁 data/
│   ├── 📁 input/        raw, never modified by code
│   └── 📁 output/       cleaned, analysis-ready
├── 📁 code/
│   ├── 📁 data-build/   input → output
│   └── 📁 analysis/     output → results
├── 📁 results/
│   ├── 📁 tables/
│   └── 📁 figures/
├── 📁 background/       literature, PDFs
├── 📁 notes/            planning, decisions
└── 📁 scratch/          throwaway
```
:::


# Project folders

- Project need not start out perfectly organized
- Think of the folder/file structure as your kitchen
    - It will get dirty
    - Don't let it get so dirty that you forget stuff
    - Clean up regularly!


# Organizing Others' Research {background-color="#23373B"}

# Reading papers

We read lots of papers. That's part of the job and critical to doing good work, and the notes you take on them are worth keeping.

:::: {.cards .two}
::: {.card}
**📝 Where the PDFs and notes live**

- OneNote "learning" notebook
- Several Mac/iPad options
- Research Rabbit
- ReMarkable tablet (my strategy)
:::
::: {.card}
**⚡ Digesting papers faster**

- Elicit
- Semantic Scholar
- Scholarcy
:::
::::


# Citation managers

Zotero, Mendeley, and EndNote Web all work. Mine is Zotero, and the bibliography flows one way:

::::: {.flow}
:::: {.step}
📚

**Zotero**

Cloud backup, every PDF linked to its citation
::::
:::: {.arrow}
→
::::
:::: {.step}
📄

**BibTeX_Library.bib**

One exported file, kept up to date on the desktop
::::
:::: {.arrow}
→
::::
:::: {.step}
☁️

**Cloud sync**

The same file on every machine
::::
:::: {.arrow}
→
::::
:::: {.step}
✍️

**Overleaf / Quarto**

Pulled into every paper, never edited by hand
